chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:
I asked him about men and women, how is the prayer offered for them? He said: The men are in front of the women, facing the Imam; they are lined up one behind the other.

key_terms.يُصَفُّ: They are lined up / arranged in rows
key_terms.يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِمْ: Prayer is offered for them (funeral prayer)

ai.seo_question: How are men and women arranged during the funeral prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the spatial hierarchy in funeral prayers, specifying that men form rows directly in front of the Imam while women stand behind them, a practice rooted in the general principle of male leadership in congregational worship. Scholars note that this arrangement reflects the social and spiritual roles assigned in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing order and modesty during communal rites. The hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding the physical structure of Salat al-Janazah in Shia tradition.
